Hi Nora —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a short lattice proposal plus a single-sheet pricing grid (redwood_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx) that summarizes numbers. Summary below — this is structured to keep BrightByte's cash flexibility while giving meaningful per-token discounts as committed volume rises.

High-level proposal (tokens per year):
- Starter: 100M tokens/year — per-token list $0.0008 -> committed price $0.00072 (10% off)
- Growth: 1.2B tokens/year — per-token list $0.0008 -> committed price $0.00056 (30% off)
- Enterprise: 4B tokens/year — per-token list $0.0008 -> committed price $0.00040 (50% off)

Mechanics and noteworthy points:
- Consumption-first: billed monthly against the annual committed amount. Unused commit at year-end converts to 60% credit for the next year if a renewal is signed within 45 days.
- Overage: flat overage price at $0.0009/token (no tiering) after committed buckets exhausted; overage counts toward next-year's committed baseline for renewals.
- Blended examples (50% draw): Starter -> $0.00076/token effective, Growth -> $0.00068/token, Enterprise -> $0.00056/token (see attached sheet for more exact math).
- SLA-linked uplift: an extra 5% discount on committed price available if BrightByte takes the Standard SLA (99.9% regional uptime) and agrees to a quarterly usage review.
- Multi-year: additional 7% off committed price on a 2-year locked renewal.

Why the lattice shape? We avoid sharp cliffs by:
- offering a modest Starter discount to reduce friction,
- giving Growth a sweet spot for scale-ups,
- and deep Enterprise discounts to justify capacity reservations and predictability on our side.

Attachments: redwood_usage_lattice_QA.pdf (walkthrough + Q&A), redwood_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx (numbers).

Next steps I recommend: brief sync (30 min) with procurement + CFO; Karthik can join to map billing and contract.
